concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor supplied no new admissible evidence that the below-target pharmacy prior-authorization issue is resolved, immaterial, or covered by approved risk acceptance/disclosure.
The Actor conceded the mitigation artifact is incomplete. No approved mitigation with the required owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion was added.
The Actor acknowledged the disclosure mismatch, but no corrected final model-card or other admissible disclosure artifact was provided.

The Actor narrowed the claim and no longer treats public governance guidance as sufficient for clean certification. That fixes part of the overbroad argument, but it does not add policy-linked evidence or close the underlying compliance gap.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor added no new admissible evidence. The response mainly reframed the same record into a narrower and more defensible position: not clean certification, but a caveated readiness posture. That reinterpretation is directionally accurate, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat corresponds to an unresolved policy predicate, not merely a disclosure nuance. The admissible record still lacks evidence of either current resolution of the material weakness or an approved mitigation/risk-acceptance path meeting the stated policy requirements, and it still lacks a corrected disclosure artifact. A narrowed narrative can make the audit packet more accurate, but accuracy of the narrative is not the same as satisfying the certification standard.
remaining_concerns: The pharmacy prior-authorization slice remains below target in a named launch use case, and there is no admissible materiality closure, approved risk acceptance, or resolution evidence.
The mitigation runbook is still draft and lacks required governance fields, including owner and alert threshold; the record also does not show an approved mitigation satisfying the policy standard.
The disclosure record remains misaligned: the draft model card says there are no known material limitations, while the admissible record shows an unresolved limitation that may require disclosure.
The narrowed actor position is more accurate, but it is still a reframing of the same evidence rather than proof that the policy predicates for certification have been met.
